result.verdict: AMBER — RED on ownership, GREEN on dependency direction and motion. The r1 Codex file's RED grade survives but NONE of its stated reasons do: its motion/PRM finding is materially false (6/6 producer motion tokens live; PRM clamps 0.57s->0.1s AND strikes transform/max-height from transition-property), its "local duplicate" is a repo-wide singleton (grep returns exactly 1 file), its central prop citation names a prop that does not exist (`type` — the prop is `variant`), and its prescribed producer contract (toast) is structurally wrong (Toaster is viewport-anchored; Chip is the fitting atom). Four new defects r1 never reached, three visible only with the stack running: L-1 MAJOR the success rung forks the sealed tone register while the error rung one line away matches `--destructive` byte-exactly (light ΔL=0.093, dark ΔC=0.023; `--color-success` bridge exists and was available); L-2 MAJOR the G-DEMO-3b boundary that `browser/index.ts:6-7` claims "enforces it standing" is wholly inert (globs name the deleted `demo/@` tree, banned specifier `@components/...` has 0 live imports, `no-restricted-imports` resolves UNSET across the entire palettes tree); L-3 MAJOR the `cardRefs` imperative registry has no teardown contract — the `el &&` guard swallows Vue's null-on-unmount, so entries are retained forever and a verdict addressed to a dead instance throws nothing, renders nothing, logs nothing (measured: 2 entries vs 1 mounted card, verdict silently lost); L-4 MAJOR the three-prop surface carries no verdict identity, so a second verdict inherits the first's clock and lives 701ms of its designed 2500ms (28%). Plus L-5/L-6/L-7 MINOR/INFO. Four superlatives proven, chiefly S-1 (pure sink: 2 imports, both external, zero relative reaches — cannot cycle) and S-2 (the producer PRM policy surgically strips transform/max-height while preserving a 100ms fade). L-3+L-4 are one repair: hoist an identity-carrying verdict object into pane state, deleting both registries, both `(el: any)` casts, the `defineExpose`, the leak, the silent-loss path and the clock bug. 5 re-runnable probes under evidence-r2/, all deterministic on cold re-run; canonical r1 file verified byte-identical to its recorded closure hash (untouched).

newDefects: L-1 MAJOR — Tone-axis fork, asymmetric within one class array. ActionFeedback.vue:8 renders the success rung from raw Tailwind literals (`bg-green-500/10 text-green-600 dark:text-green-400`) while :9 renders the error rung from the producer token (`bg-destructive/10 text-destructive`). Measured live: error ink rgb(219,36,36) === `--destructive` byte-exactly; success ink oklch(0.627 0.194 149.214) vs `--success` oklch(0.72 0.192 149.5) (ΔL=0.093); dark arm oklch(0.792 0.209 151.711) vs the token's own dark arm oklch(0.805 0.186 151.6) (ΔC=0.023). Unforced — glass-ui bridges `--color-success: var(--success)` in dist/styles/theme/bridges.css, and `--success` is already light-dark(), so the hand-rolled `dark:` variant is a second, divergent dark-mode mechanism for a token that never needed one. Also violates the sealed axis in dist/components/_shared/axes.d.ts three ways: prop NAME (`variant` carrying tone, which the axis comment forbids explicitly), VOCABULARY (`error` is not in TONES; the producer word is `destructive`), and RENDERING. Repro: evidence-r2/af-L-r2-tone-fork.mjs. Not a contrast regression (forked ink is darker) — the defect is ownership: two sources of truth for "success", only one of which moves with the design system.

L-2 MAJOR — The barrel seam cited as enforced is inert; blast radius is the whole palette-browser feature. demo/palettes/browser/index.ts:6-7 asserts the G-DEMO-3b eslint boundary "enforces it standing". It enforces nothing: (a) the rule's files globs (eslint.config.js:232-238) name demo/@/components, demo/@/lib, demo/@/composables — `demo/@` does not exist, the feature lives at demo/palettes/browser/, matched by no glob; (b) the banned specifier `@components/custom/palette-browser/**/*.vue` is unresolvable, `grep -rn 'from "@components' demo/ src/` returns 0, with vite.config.ts:68 recording that W43·RF-15 killed the demo `@…` aliases; (c) `npx eslint --print-config` returns `no-restricted-imports: UNSET` for BrowsePane.vue, PalettesPane.vue, ActionFeedback.vue AND browser/index.ts itself. The one surviving glob (demo/color-picker/**) loads the rule to guard a dead address. Directly on-seat: ActionFeedback is exported by no barrel (correctly — a true internal), and the mechanism claimed to keep it internal died at the W43 restructure. Repro: evidence-r2/af-L-r2-boundary-inert.sh.

L-3 MAJOR — The imperative channel has no teardown contract; verdicts addressed to unmounted cards are silently lost. PalettesPane.vue:84 and BrowsePane.vue:94 register via `:ref="(el: any) => el && (cardRefs[key] = el)"`. Vue invokes a function ref with null on unmount; the `el &&` guard swallows that call, so entries are never deleted. Measured by filtering one card out through the pane's own search box: cardRefKeys stays ["af-probe-1","af-probe-2"] while mountedCards drops to 1, retainedDead ["af-probe-2"]. L-3a the registry grows monotonically retaining unmounted instances across a session of searching/filtering/deleting/paging. L-3b calling showFeedback on a retained-dead instance — exactly what PalettesPane.vue:207 and BrowsePane.vue:249 do after an await — throws nothing, renders nothing, logs nothing (chipsOnScreen 0, threw null, console/page errors []). The user's publish/save/delete/fork outcome vanishes. BrowsePane.vue:249/:264 guard absence with `?.` but never deadness. The `(el: any)` cast defeats the registry's declared `Record<string, InstanceType<typeof PaletteCard>>` at the one site where the contract could be checked. Repro: evidence-r2/af-L-r2-registry-leak.mjs.

L-4 MAJOR — The public surface carries no verdict identity, so a second verdict inherits the first one's clock. Ownership is split across the seam: visibility state in the parent (PaletteCard.vue:234-236), dismissal clock in the child (ActionFeedback.vue:37-47), whose only re-arm trigger is a change-watcher on a boolean. showFeedback (PaletteCard.vue:238-242) sets feedbackVisible = true unconditionally, so a second verdict arriving while the first chip is up does not CHANGE `visible`, the watcher never fires, and the 2500ms clock is never re-armed. Measured trace: A shown t≈102ms; B shown t≈2158ms; chip null by t≈2859ms; still null t≈3859ms — B lived ~701ms, 28% of its designed lifetime. The failure scales precisely with the traffic it exists to report on. Repro: evidence-r2/af-L-r2-no-verdict-identity.mjs.

L-5 MINOR — Name, location and coupling disagree. Domain-coupling census across the six-file folder: PaletteCard.vue 364L/55 palette-refs, PaletteCardMenu 228L/23, PaletteCardMeta 64L/17, PaletteRenameInput 66L/1, PaletteCardSwatches 96L/1, ActionFeedback 58L/0. It is the only file with zero domain coupling and the only one lacking a `Palette*` prefix — its name claims app-wide generality, its location claims card-locality, its content is domain-free with exactly one consumer. Verdict on the decomposition itself: the six-file split is along REAL seams, not a distributed god module. Per feedback_kiss_no_contrivance the cure is a rename to PaletteCardFeedback.vue, NOT relocation to demo/shared/ui/ — a single-consumer leaf does not earn a shared home.

L-6 MINOR — A producer atom exists and is hand-rolled here instead. ActionFeedback.vue:7 hand-rolls `flex items-center gap-2 px-3 py-1.5 rounded-panel text-xs`; glass-ui Chip (dist/components/chip/) ships mode:"static" + tone + size + shape:"pill", with chipVariants sm = "gap-1 px-2.5 py-1 text-caption" — the same recipe. Chip has exactly ONE adopter repo-wide (demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/easing/EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:14), so this is live under-adoption. Producer relay (BJ ask): Chip's tone is typed `tone?: string` in dist/components/chip/types.d.ts rather than the `Tone` the producer seals in _shared/axes.d.ts — part of why consumers keep inventing their own tone vocabularies.

L-7 INFO — 25% of the public prop surface is dead. `autoDismissMs` (ActionFeedback.vue:28, default 2500) is bound by no consumer; PaletteCard.vue:123-128 passes only message, variant, visible and @update:visible. A configuration point with zero configurers — delete it or make it load-bearing when the L-4 verdict object lands.

OUT-OF-SEAT (D axis, observed live in every probe run, recorded so it is not lost) — the chip renders role: null and aria-live: null. Verdicts for publish/save/delete/fork are never announced to assistive technology.

result.verdict: LIVE-RED · BLOCKER ×2. The prior Codex file was cosmetically half-right and missed every defect that actually breaks the instrument. Measured live: (1) `--z-debug` is the ONE rung of the demo's z-ladder that resolves to nothing (`--z-behind`…`--z-modal` all resolve; `--z-debug` UNDEFINED), so `PointerDebugOverlay.vue:136` computes `z-index: auto` and loses to `.pane-wrapper--left { z-index: 1 }` — at 1440×900 the FROZEN? alarm, the copied! confirmation, the collapse glyph and every gauge VALUE are 100% occluded. This is a REGRESSION: production (color.babb.dev) resolves `--z-debug: 99999` and renders correctly; the token was deleted by commit c84504d3 on a glass-ui-bridges-it premise that glass-ui does not honour. (2) At 390×844 — the phone, the only platform this iOS-Safari pointer-capture instrument exists for — the header is 97.5% occluded and absent from the hit-test stack, so a trusted tap cannot collapse it: expand is IRREVERSIBLE. (3) 91.4% of the event log is unreachable — `.debug-scroll` carries `pointer-events: none` + `tabIndex -1`, so trusted wheel, trusted drag and keyboard all leave `scrollTop` at 0 with 2586px hidden and 2 of 80 rows visible. (4) The activation gate is a raw substring match with no build gate: `?nodebug=1` turns debug ON, and `https://color.babb.dev/?nodebug=1` renders the overlay to the public product. Answering the seat's framing question with evidence: as gated and as built, this UI should not ship — it is production-reachable by accident and does not work when reached. Five superlatives proved to the same standard, incl. the correct default-collapsed geometry, word-not-colour boolean gauges that survive forced-colors, and the pointer-events discipline that keeps the instrument from perturbing what it measures.

reAdjudications.claim: D#1 — `aria-controls="debug-body"` references no element; the disclosure's structural relationship is false
D#2 (composite) — a 280px fixed overlay at bottom-left can cover essential phone UI and ignores safe-area insets, keyboard, RTL, and drag/reposition needs
D#2a (rider) — ignores safe-area insets
D#2b (rider) — ignores RTL
D#2c (rider, the headline) — the overlay covers essential phone UI
D#3 — 10px type and 6px button padding are too small for extended reading and touch operation
D#4 — `FROZEN?` blinks every 0.5s forever; there is no reduced-motion rule; the question mark weakens a diagnostic assertion
D#5 — copy success is transient text inside the header without status semantics; failure is never shown
D#6 — Reset, Copy JSON and Clear have equal geometry although Reset is destructive and can alter the very fault under inspection
D#7 — hard-coded black/white/red/blue styling forms a separate visual system with no forced-colors/high-contrast contract

newDefects: D-N1 · BLOCKER — `--z-debug` is the sole orphaned rung of the demo z-ladder (all of --z-behind/-background/-content/-controls/-ornament/-bar/-header/-dock/-overlay/-popover/-modal resolve; --z-debug UNDEFINED), so PointerDebugOverlay.vue:136 computes `z-index: auto` and is overpainted by `.pane-wrapper--left { z-index: 1 }`. Measured occlusion at 1440×900: `.debug-frozen` 100%, `.debug-toggle` 100%, `.debug-copied` 100%, first `.debug-gauge .debug-val` 100%, whole overlay 30.1% — and the occluded 30% is exactly the value column (`justify-content: space-between`). REGRESSION: production resolves `--z-debug: 99999` and renders every value; the token was deleted from `:root` by commit c84504d3 (2026-03-25) on the premise at foundation.css:110 that glass-ui bridges it — glass-ui defines no `--z-*` at all. Evidence 02 vs 03.

D-N2 · BLOCKER — mobile collapse trap. At 390×844 the expanded `.debug-header` (9, 676.4, 278, 30.2) is 97.5% occluded by the picker card; `document.elementsFromPoint(148, 691.5)` returns `DIV.channel-rows.flex-1` (header absent from the hit-test stack); a real trusted `mouse.click` at the header centre leaves `aria-expanded="true"` and the class un-collapsed; Playwright actionability times out. Expand is irreversible on the one platform the instrument exists for. Evidence 08b, 09.

D-N3 · MAJOR — the event log is 91.4% unreachable by every input modality. `.debug-scroll` (PointerDebugOverlay.vue:232-237) is `overflow-y: auto` + `pointer-events: none`, `tabIndex -1`. With the 80-event ring full: scrollHeight 2829 / clientHeight 243 / hidden 2586px; trusted wheel → scrollTop 0; trusted drag → scrollTop 0; keyboard PageDown/End with the header focused → scrollTop 0; hit-test over the log returns `MAIN.pane-main`. Only 2 of 80 rows are ever visible; Chromium paints a scrollbar no user can move.

D-N4 · MAJOR — the activation gate is a raw substring match with no build gate. usePointerDebug.ts:34-39 uses `location.hash.includes("debug=1") || location.search.includes("debug=1")`. Live: `?nodebug=1` → ON, `?xdebug=1` → ON, `?q=notdebug=1x` → ON, `#/palettes?ref=mydebug=1` → ON; controls `?debug=0` and `/` → OFF. No `import.meta.env.DEV` guard, so it ships: `https://color.babb.dev/?nodebug=1` renders the overlay to the public product, wiring 6 document capture listeners + a 500ms interval and a one-tap destructive Reset.

D-N5 · MAJOR — no state has accessible structure. Live AX tree: `role: null`, `aria-label: null` on `.debug-overlay`; `liveRegions: 0` (no aria-live/status/alert/log), so FROZEN and copied! are both silent; the entire 80-row payload arrives as one flat `text:` run with no heading/list/table semantics and no key↔value association; the disclosure's accessible name mutates with state ("Debug −" → "Debug FROZEN? −" → "Debug copied! −"); the three action buttons carry no `type` attribute.

D-N6 · MINOR — measured WCAG AA 1.4.3 contrast failure in the seat's own bytes: `.debug-val-false` (`#666`, 10px, PointerDebugOverlay.vue:229) = 3.47:1 against the composited panel `rgb(16, 5.6, 17.2)` — the FALSE state of every boolean gauge. (Adjacent, DebugEventLog-owned, relayed: `.debug-ts` #666 = 3.47:1, `.debug-tgt` #777 = 4.45:1.)

D-N7 · MINOR — the disclosure has no authored focus treatment: no `.debug-header:focus-visible` rule exists (only `.debug-btn:focus-visible` at :270-273), so the header falls back to Chrome's UA `outline: auto 1px rgb(0,95,204)` on a near-black panel, while the app's own `.focus-ring` utility (which carries a forced-colors contract) goes unused.

D-N8 · INFO — the clipboard export (buildExportJSON, :82-107) embeds `navigator.userAgent` verbatim plus screen dimensions and DPR; combined with D-N4 this is a public, production-reachable surface that puts an environment fingerprint on a stranger's clipboard on one tap, confirmed only by an occluded chip.

D-N9 · INFO — the four debug controls are tab stops 26–29 of 30 (teleported to the end of body); a keyboard operator traverses the whole app to reach the instrument, and expanding it moves focus nowhere.

D-N10 · INFO (epistemic record, not scored) — one captured unattended full-frame navigation `…/?debug=1#/` → `…/#/browse` at ~16.5s that dropped the flag and unmounted the overlay. Did NOT reproduce: a clean 25s idle poll held the flag, and deliberate Picker→Palettes→Home navigation preserved both flag and overlay. Trigger unidentified; possible dev-server interference. Recorded because the flag has no durable state and no in-product re-entry.

result.verdict: DEFECTIVE — 15 findings (2 BLOCKER, 6 MAJOR, 5 MINOR, 2 INFO) plus 5 proven superlatives, all measured live against http://localhost:9000 at HEAD 0b4566db with 13 re-runnable probes, 12 JSON receipts and 46 PNG witnesses under evidence-r2/. Four of the five clauses of the component's own stated design thesis (ConsoleRail.vue:2-11) are false in the build. Canonical challenge-D-design.md untouched (sha b5c098449351a274593c421938c7e50633811f9d09d11921855e81bfeb7bf48f); no source file modified.

reAdjudications.claim: Codex D#1 — role=tablist/role=tab implies associated tabpanels, but no aria-controls or panel relationship exists; if selection merely scrolls a slider row, a radio/listbox or toolbar pattern may be more honest
Codex D#2 — single glyphs (C, h, a, b, α) require tooltip discovery; the visible rail alone does not communicate units, ranges, or which color space is active
Codex D#3 — when `active` is invalid rather than null, no tab receives tabindex=0 and keyboard entry into the rail becomes uncertain
Codex D#4 — the live-color dot can become visually dominant or noisy across rapid color changes; no reduced-motion/high-contrast/forced-colors design is stated
Codex D#5 — tooltips remain the primary explanation; touch users have no persistent anatomy legend, and long localized descriptions are constrained to max-w-56
Codex D#6 — the vertical chassis assumes enough height to distribute every channel; dense spaces, landscape phones, and large text can compress or overflow it

Codex 'Required Kronecker cells' paragraph — Spaces × 1–5 channels × selected/null/invalid × dark/light/forced-colors × keyboard/touch/pointer × reduced-motion × phone portrait/landscape/desktop × short/long localized labels
